title: Such an insane concept that I knew I absolutely had to go-if not only...
transcript: What do you get when you mix the office with The Great Gatsby? Well, you get Gatz, an eight hour. Yes, eight hour show in which they recite the entirety of The Great Gatsby novel verbatim. They do it in four parts with three breaks, including a 90 minute dinner break. So where does the office come in? the other unique thing about Gatz is that it takes place in a modern American office. The show begins with our main character, who is unnamed, picking up a copy of The Great Gatsby and beginning to read it as a means of passing the time at work. And as he becomes more invested in the novel, the world of Gatsby slowly comes to life around him, with his coworkers taking on key roles in the novel. And this draws some interesting parallels between the hierarchy of the office and the social hierarchy of the 1920s and the Great Gatsby novel. And so, while they are not changing a single word in the text, they are still able to overlay this meta commentary that is really clever in ways that I wasn't expecting. And of course, they also have a lot of fun with how they stage certain scenes, always just using found items in the office, which leads to a lot of moments of comedy and does feel very sitcom esque at times. And I feel like I should point out that this actually predates the US version of The Office, the theater company that created Gatz is Elevator Repair Service, and they actually started development on the show in 1999 and have been performing it on and off since 2004 and has since become one of those legendary theater experiences that I honestly think everyone should see at some point, if not just to say that you saw it. I know that it can be hard to give up basically a full day just for one show, and while it can certainly be a slog at times, I really do think it is worth your time.
reasoning: Creator calls it a legendary theater experience everyone should see, praises the clever meta commentary and staging, and explicitly says it's worth your time despite the length.
